messages:
mira: quick follow-up to the canary RFC — proposing a 'decision shim' that lives next to the router to make local fallback decisions. thinking: decentralize fast decisions, keep control plane authoritative for policy.

sam: curious, how is this different from the probe-based controller we discussed last week?

mira: good q. probe controller is centralized and issues route changes. shim makes per-request decisions (switch to fallback variant, mirror, or retry) based on local signals + latest policy snapshot. controller still ships snapshots and audit events.

jiwon: sounds useful for latency-sensitive fallbacks. main worry: split-brain between shim decisions and control plane rollouts. how do we avoid inconsistent user experiences?

mira: plan: 1) policy has version + min-cohort flag, 2) shim enforces policy version bounds and will only apply local heuristics if snapshot fresh (<30s) or if policy allows autonomous heuristics.

rafa: what heuristics are we talking about? e.g., error-rate over last N, p95 latency spike, or queue-depth?

mira: yes — short-window error-rate, moving-p95, and kv-cache-miss-ratio. simple weighted score, thresholded. We intentionally keep heuristics simple to avoid tuning hell.

ellen: how do we handle observability and audits? need to trace decisions back to policy snapshots and metrics that triggered fallback.

mira: all decisions emit an event to the control plane event-writer: ``{kind: "shim_decision", policy_v: 42, reason: "p95>200ms", sample_metrics: {...}}``. shim also tags traces with policy_v and decision.

sam: what's the failure mode if the shim goes rogue (bad config / bug) and routes 100% traffic to a degraded fallback?

mira: two defenses: 1) circuit breaker in the router that falls back to control-plane enforced routing if shim decision rate exceeds safe delta, 2) rollout budget enforced centrally — any shim override must respect per-tenant budget tokens.

jiwon: budget tokens? can you sketch the interface?

mira: sketch: ``GET /policy/{tenant} -> {v: 42, autonomy: true, override_budget: 100}`` ; shim consumes tokens each time it overrides routing. control plane refills tokens based on SLA and operator config.

rafa: conceptually nice. overhead concerns: extra network call to control plane on every change?

mira: no. snapshots are pushed and cached. tokens are small counters refreshed opportunistically. only audit events are batched to reduce egress.

ellen: testing: can we run shim in "observe-only" mode for a week to collect decision telemetry without affecting production?

mira: yes — rollout plan: observe-only -> shadow overrides (no consumer impact) -> limited autonomy (1% tenants) -> graduated. deploy-bot: canary started in cluster eu-west-1 (sha: b17c3). :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment initiated for shim v1.1. Observability hooks: /dash/shim-decisions, logs: gcs://redwood/shim/canary/1749991111

sam: one more tradeoff: complexity at the edge vs mental model for app owners. docs need to be crystal about what "autonomy" means and failure modes.

mira: agreed. I'll draft a short owner-facing doc and an RFC appendix on invariants. Also planning a small API: ``/policy/preview?tenant=x`` so owners can simulate shard-local decisions.

jiwon: lgtm. can we add a kill-switch that ops can flip cluster-wide?

mira: already on it — central kill-switch + per-tenant force-control flag.

rafa: scheduling follow-up: can we sync tomorrow 10am to review the shim state machine and token semantics?

ellen: i'll join. can you add a quick state diagram to the PR? even ascii is fine.

mira: will do. thanks all.
